replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: Yes, especially when tackling complex problems without clear steps. My high neuroticism score makes me prone to stress during high-pressure scenarios like exams. But I use deep breathing and break problems into smaller parts to stay calm.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: I used AI tools like Wolfram Alpha to check my calculus solutions and generate step-by-step explanations. It helped me understand concepts faster, but I was cautious about over-reliance, ensuring I still practiced manually to build intuition.
replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, write the equation in standard form ax² + bx + c = 0. Then, calculate the discriminant b² - 4ac. If positive, you get two real roots; zero means one real root; negative means complex roots. Use the quadratic formula x = [-b ± √(b²-4ac)] / (2a) to find them.

To find stationary points, take the first derivative f'(x), set it equal to zero, and solve for x. Plug those x-values back into f(x) to get the corresponding y-values. These points are where the slope of the function is zero, indicating local maxima or minima.
replies.Briefly, how do you perform a Principal: PCA reduces data dimensions by identifying directions (principal components) that capture the most variance.
